statement: For independent nearest-neighbor bond percolation on S_k=Z x {-k,...,k}, k a nonnegative integer, p_c(S_k)=1. For 0<=p<1 and R>=1, P_p((0,0) connects to a vertex with |x|>=R) <= 2[1-(1-p)^(2k+1)]^R.

source.primary_source_status: self-contained elementary derivation; accepted source tag confirmed against BUNDLE_SPEC

proof: Each interface between adjacent columns has 2k+1 bonds. Its all-closed event has probability q=(1-p)^(2k+1); distinct interfaces have disjoint edge sets. Reaching x=R requires avoiding R independent cuts, and similarly for x=-R. Union bound gives the displayed estimate. As R tends to infinity the probability of an infinite origin cluster vanishes. Countability treats every vertex. At p=1 the strip is connected and infinite.
remaining_gap: No gap in the elementary strip proof identified; independent review pending. This does not prove the original C0023 statement.

statement: Let G be infinite, connected and locally finite, and let G_n be increasing subgraphs containing o and exhausting all vertices and edges of G. At a fixed common Bernoulli bond parameter p, write a_n(R)=P_p(o connects in G_n to ambient graph distance at least R). Then theta_G(p)=inf_R sup_n a_n(R), whereas theta_G_n(p)=inf_R a_n(R). Consequently theta_G(p)=0 iff for every epsilon>0 there exists R such that for every n, a_n(R)<=epsilon.
assumptions: infinite connected locally finite ambient graph
increasing vertex-and-edge exhaustion with common origin
fixed parameter and common coupled edge law
proof: Every finite-path witness is included in some exhausting subgraph, giving continuity from below at fixed R. Ambient finite-radius balls are finite, so decreasing one-arm events intersect exactly in the infinite-cluster event; continuity from above gives the identity and its epsilon quantifiers. The argument does not multiply dependent events.
remaining_gap: Independent mathematical check pending; no estimate uniform in slab width at the original critical parameter has been proved.

statement: Unrestricted passage of nonpercolation through an increasing graph exhaustion is false even for infinite connected locally finite quasi-transitive nearest-neighbor graphs. At p=99/100, every strip S_k=Z x {-k,...,k} has theta_Sk(p)=0, but their union Z^2 has theta_Z2(p)>=1-10557/2352250000>0.99999.
assumptions: independent nearest-neighbor Bernoulli bonds on Z^2
same fixed p=99/100 in every graph
finite k before the radius limit
counterexample: Finite strip cuts prove theta_Sk(p)=0. A finite origin cluster in the plane forces an enclosing closed dual circuit of length m>=4. There are at most 4m*3^(m-1) such circuits. The union bound gives finite-cluster probability <=(4/3)*a^4*(4-3a)/(1-a)^2, a=3(1-p)=3/100, which equals 10557/2352250000. Thus sup_k inf_R a_k(R)=0 but inf_R sup_k a_k(R)>0.99999.
remaining_gap: Independent check of the planar boundary/counting argument pending. This example is supercritical in the plane, and strip critical thresholds do not converge to the planar threshold; it does not refute the original critical target or a bridge with additional threshold-convergence assumptions.

statement: In the four-cycle o--a--b--c--o with relays A={a,c}, no deterministic vertex v and relay a_star satisfy both separator assumptions of w426 L1. This obstructs that finite-forest proof extension, not the product gluing inequality.
assumptions: Undirected four-cycle with four distinct vertices
counterexample: The direct o-to-a and o-to-c paths share only o, so their common separator must be o. The direct edge from either relay to b avoids o. At p=1/2 exact enumeration still gives terminal probability 7/16 above product bound 27/64.
